requirements.requirement: On node1, require new passwords to be at least 12 characters long and contain at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: A root-owned pwquality drop-in sets minlen=12 and minclass=3. Direct PAM tests rejected an 11-character password and a 12-character/two-class password without changing the credential, while accepting a compliant password. The configuration and equivalent behavior remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The implementation used the already-installed PAM/libpwquality stack, whose versions remained unchanged, and package health was intact afterward.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Password length and character-class enforcement was demonstrated through the real PAM password-change path, persisted across restart, and the platform was preserved. The mandatory node1 restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered services and access, preserved data, and matching lifecycle cross-checks were all captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The persistent pwquality drop-in directly implemented the task. Temporary password files, the probe account and its credential changes were bounded functional-verification prerequisites; the account, files, group, and initially missed empty mail spool were subsequently removed. Temporary final-evidence files were trap-cleaned, and the restart was required by the provider-wide protocol. The failed passwd and openssl-based attempts provide no evidence of retained state changes. Final observations show no failed units, no probe residue, unchanged protected-file checksums, healthy package state, and only expected reboot-related PID and temporary-directory changes.
